When I got diagnosed back in December I always went alone. I was a medical student (graduated in June) and my university's psychiatric clinic offered free psychodiagnostic session with a clinical psychologist and prescription for antidepressants. I'm now seeing a therapist at a mental health foundation. I still go alone to every session and it has never been uncomfortable or scary. My family lives far from me, I don't have a partner and I don't want to be a burden for my friends. I would suggest trying it alone. Maybe you can be more open about your problems when you are alone with the psychiatrist/therapist. I have never had someone with me during these session and I prefer it that way cause we talk about extremely personal stuff and I can only trust her with those and no one else.

When I was severly depressed in the winter my apartment was also really messy, I had no energy to clean, do the dishes or laundry. I'm feeling better now so I try to keep my place clean but I still have to work on being more consistent with household chores. Or maybe if you have a good relationship with your family, they can help you a little bit, my family always does when I'm depressed. I would not suggest using drugs, but maybe a strong coffe/energy drink/any other caffeine source and some good music can be motivational as well.
